extracted.intended_audience: Tenure-track assistant professors (early-career faculty) in CBET/ENG considering NSF CAREER proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing an NSF CAREER proposal in CBET (Division of Chemical, Bioengineering, Environmental, and Transport Systems), emphasizing integrated research, education, and outreach over a five-year budget period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Sheet Title requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "CAREER:" in Title
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover sheet should identify the proposal as a CAREER submission by including 'CAREER:' in the title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch (2 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical Sketch limited to 2 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Research and Education Accomplishments in the biographical sketch; adhere to the 2-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary (1 page)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary must be one page and address both Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise statements for both review criteria (Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts) on this single page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental Letter (2 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departmental letter limited to 2 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter should describe activities supported by the institution and the career development of the PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description (15 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Description up to 15 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include the Proposed Research Project & Plan, Proposed Education Activities, Integration with Research, and Assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget limits and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Five years, $500,000 total
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a budget request consistent with a five-year CAREER award and the $500,000 total guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated Research & Education Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: CAREER proposals must have an integrated research & education plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose creative research and education plans and explicitly describe how they will be integrated and assessed. Explain how the research program will impact educational goals and how education activities will feed back to research. Balance research and education (quality over quantity) and avoid over-proposing activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the proposed activities will contribute to disciplinary or interdisciplinary understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe potential societal benefits, outreach, education, or other impacts beyond the research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity / Originality / Transformative Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for novel ideas and potential for significant change in the field; highlight originality and transformative aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-reasoned Plan & Assessment Mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-reasoned, well-organized plan based on a sound rationale; does the plan incorporate a mechanism to assess success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the rationale, organization, methods, and include explicit mechanisms for assessing both research progress and education/outreach effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of the PI
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications of PI to conduct the proposed activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document prior accomplishments, relevant expertise, and capacity to carry out the integrated research and education plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate Institutional and Collaborator Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate resources available to PI/PI team at home/collaborator institution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe facilities, institutional support, and collaborator commitments that enable successful completion of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement and contribution of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancement and contribution of knowledge in its own field or across different disciplines?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate expected contributions to scholarship or cross-disciplinary advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-conceived and organized proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the proposal well-conceived and organized?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the narrative clearly, with coherent aims, methods, and a timeline consistent with the five-year vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of teaching, training, & learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancement of discovery and understanding while promoting teaching, training, & learning?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the research program will enhance pedagogy, student training, and learning outcomes (e.g., graduate, undergraduate, K-12 involvement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad dissemination and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad dissemination to enhance scientific and technological understanding, e.g. Outreach?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for sharing results widely (publications, conferences, outreach activities) and how dissemination contributes to broader impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening participation of under-represented groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation of under-represented groups in STEM?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include targeted activities to engage and support under-represented groups; explain metrics or plans to measure participation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational Impact (undergraduate & K-12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational Impact, including undergraduate & K-12?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail specific education/outreach programming, target audiences (e.g., K-12, undergraduate), and expected educational outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page allocation & expectations for Research vs Education sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Research (10-12 pages) and Education (3-5 pages) recommended length and content expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research section should present a five-year vision with aims, significance, methods, and a plan for sustained contribution; Education section should be 3–5 pages showing education/outreach activities inspired by the research, integrated with it, with plans for assessment and engagement of under-represented groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision for five-year program and lifetime contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision for five year research & education program for a lifetime of contributions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate how the CAREER award will launch a sustained program of scholarship and educational leadership over the PI's career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and evaluation of education activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Are these activities assessed and evaluated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an evaluation plan for education/outreach activities. An outside evaluator is not required, but some evaluation mechanism is expected; use institutional resources or collaborators if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — faculty rank/time window
rubrics_metrics.description: Only assistant professors without tenure are eligible; appointment status as of the effective date matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must be an assistant professor (or equivalent) without tenure and remain in that rank until the October 1 following the proposal submission deadline. If your appointment becomes Associate Professor on or before that date you are not eligible. Do not submit if you anticipate a title change before that cutoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return without review triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Which items will lead to return without review: listing a co-PI; PI did not submit to the current CAREER solicitation; departmental letter missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure no co-principal investigators are listed, submit to the current CAREER solicitation, and include the required departmental letter to avoid return without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: One CAREER proposal per competition
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit only one CAREER proposal per competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit multiple CAREER proposals to different programs/divisions/directorates in the same competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: No duplicate/substantially similar concurrent submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: May not submit a CAREER proposal and a regular research proposal on a similar topic to NSF at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same work cannot be funded twice. Submitting duplicate or substantially similar proposals concurrently without prior NSF approval will result in return of the redundant proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of having another NSF grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Having an NSF grant when applying for CAREER does not preclude winning a CAREER award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content of the CAREER proposal must be significantly different from other active NSF proposals/grants so it does not appear to be a resubmission of the same work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary review mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: How are CAREER proposals reviewed? CAREER awards are mainly reviewed by panel review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect panel-based review as the primary review route (may include mail/ad-hoc components as used by the program).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation staffing: outside evaluator optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Do I need to involve an outside evaluator for the education component? No, an outside evaluator is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, include an evaluation plan and consider internal institutional evaluation resources (education departments or existing course evaluation systems) or collaborators to design assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting feedback from Program Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a Proposal Concept and one-page summary (Intellectual Merit & Broader Impacts) to Program Director for feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the program description on NSF website, email a one-page summary to the PD, request PD feedback by email, request a visit to NSF Arlington with dates, or request a phone call (provide list of questions by email at least 24 hours before the call). PD will provide feedback by email.
